intro.title: Write a timeout wrapper for promises
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function that wraps a promise to add a timeout, ensuring it either resolves with the original promise's result or rejects if it takes too long. You'll learn how to use JavaScript promises, the setTimeout function, and the Promise.race method to handle asynchronous operations with time limits. The main constructs involved are creating promises, managing timeouts, and combining promises to control execution flow. This is a practical skill for making your code more robust by preventing indefinite waiting in network requests or other async tasks.
intro.usecase: In real applications, network requests can hang indefinitely when servers are slow or unresponsive. A timeout wrapper for promises is essential for creating responsive user interfaces like search autocomplete fields, dashboard data fetches, and payment processing forms. For example, when users search in an e-commerce site, you want to show 'Request timed out' after 5 seconds rather than leaving them waiting forever. This pattern also prevents memory leaks in long-running operations and improves overall application reliability.
